newsitem.title: BRAZIL: RESEARCH ALERT-CRT still an ING Barings buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-CRT still an ING Barings buy.

text.p: ING Barings reiterated its buy recommendation on Brazilian state-owned telecom Cia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT) and raised its target price for the stock to $237.50 per 100 shares from $211.

-- In a report, ING Barings analyst Vera Rossi said the CRT will be the first telecom to be privatized after the Rio Grande do Sul state legislature last week approved a bill allowing the sale of a controlling stake in the firm.
-- The state, which in December sold a minority operating stake in CRT to a group including Spain's Telefonica de Espana (TISA), owns 56.2 percent of CRT.
-- "TISA does not have preferred rights to buy the remaining stake (but) will run the company for the next 10 years," Rossi wrote.
-- She also said CRT's capital expenditure program in cellular services is more advanced than its peers and it is expected to be the last firm to face competition in cellular services.
-- CRT is in a favorable positon because its privatization will occur by the end of 1997 before federal telecom holding Telebras, which is to be broken up and sold off in 1998, she said.
-- Also, the price of CRT stock should appreciate on increased liquidity when it is listed on the Sao Paulo bolsa, she said. The shares now trade on Rio de Janeiro's SOMA over-the-counter exchange.
-- ING increased its target premium for CRT over Latin American peers to 20 percent from 10 percent and raised its target stock price to $237.50 per 100 shares from $211.
-- CRT preferred A ended off 2.81 percent at 173 reais Monday while its common rose 2.99 percent to 155.10 reais.
